- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.00) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >65), then corrects — apply downward bias in next 3–5 periods.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price has been trending down for 5+ days, forecast tends to be too low; adjust upward slightly.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates true price in early periods (1–5 days) after a spike — apply upward bias to first 3–5 forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment momentum, not just price history.
